page.layout: One printed page: running head at top; main text in one full column; numbered paragraphs (4 and 5) run as text, with small notes set beside the lines in the body of the text; no margin notes outside the text block.

main_text.p: priuatim aliquid boni precari religio est. Caeterum omnibus Persis, ac regi, prosperitatem optat: quippe inter uniuersos Persas, ipse quoq; unus est. Et diuina est apud Euripidem Menaecei, se pro patria deuoturi sententia, quam adscribam, ut hic Antonini locus recte intelligatur:

Εἰ γὰρ λαβὼν ἐναγ-ῳ̂ ὅ, τι ἀμύνατο τῆς
Χρησ-τὸν, Ἀιελέοι τῆτο, ἢ ἐις κοινὸν φέρει
Πατρίδι, μακὰ ὢν ἂν ἀι πόλεις ἐλασσόνωσι
Περιφύλλαι, τὸ κοινὸν ἀντυχοίην ἂν. id est:
main_text.l: Si quilibet, quantum queat boni, lubens
Sed accident in posterum res prosperae.
main_text.p: Itaq; Athenienses iniuste & illiberaliter suis tantum agris pluuiam & fertilitatem poscebant: qui si omnibus hominibus felicitatem ac successa omnia optassent, & humanae rationem societatis habuissent, neq; communi prosperitate exclusi fuissent.
4Totum enim mutilatur.) Τὴν ἀ[?]ὰ γὰρ τὸ ὁλόκληρον: non τυφλῶς.

5Neq; tibi est ad philosophiam.) Sensus huius loci habet nonnihil obscuritatis. videtur autem haec esse sententia: Si quid instituueris agere secundum rectam rationem, & cuctus consilio tuo non respondeat, non debes idcirco tuum propositum damnare: sed potius cogitare, quam multa in rebus humanis sint, & accidere queant, quae obstent, quo minus

page.notes: Greek passages copied as legible; the Euripides line and the Greek note text contain doubtful letters and are reproduced with best reading (e.g. "ἀ[?]ὰ" in the note to 4, "ἐναγ-ῳ̂" region). Marginal number "4" and "5" stand beside their paragraphs at left. The final word "nus" is a catchword-like fragment at the foot of the column, set at the right, read as printed; it is the continuation of "minus" split across the line end. Latin word "s" forms are rendered as plain s; some Greek letters in the verse are uncertain and should be checked against the scan.
